components.title: Removal and placement of the CoEx XL brewer
components.text:
Removal procedure
Perform the following steps to remove the brewer:
1. To remove the brewer from the coffee machine, place four fingers in the lower grip (1). With your thumb, push and hold down the locking grip (2) and pull the brewer from the mounting frame in the direction of the arrow (3).
Placement procedure
Perform the following steps to install the brewer:
1. Make sure the inside of the brewer mounting frame in the coffee machine is clean.
2. Insert the brewer into the mounting frame and push until it locks.
▪All other connections are made automatically.
▪The brewer will initialize once when the first coffee
dispense is started. All brewer parts are moved to the correct starting position first.

components.title: Replace service parts in the brewer
components.text:
The only serviceable parts in the brewer that need to be replaced after 50.000 brewing cycles (or 2 years) are:
1. the coffee filter assembly with seals.
2. the inner cylinder.
3. the inlet filter assembly with seals.
A complete set is available as spare part set.
The CoEx XL serial number (visible on a heat- and water resistant label on top of the brewer gear box) contains the manufacturing date. The number format is year-week-sequence number.
Procedure
Follow the steps to replace the service parts.
1. Before removing the brewer from the machine, first place the brewer in the Service position. A service option in the Service Menu can help to do this, check the section Place brewer in service position (on page 70).
2. Remove the brewer from the machine and remove the cover from the brewer. Check the chapter 'Remove and clean the brewer' in the User manual for details.
Remove inlet filter
Follow this procedure:
1. Remove one screw (1) that secures the inlet filter. (M4/ Length=16mm)
2. Turn the inlet filter clockwise (2) to release the bayonet locking.
3. Loosen and remove the inlet filter from the piston.
Remove inner cylinder
Follow this procedure:
1. Remove 1 screw that secures the inner cylinder. (M4/ Length=16mm).
2. Turn the brewer around again.
3. Slide the inner cylinder (1) out of the outer cylinder. Tilt (2) and remove it from the brewer.
Replace coffee filter
Follow this procedure:
1. Push the cylinder down by hand.
2. If the cylinder is locked, locate the clutches on the left (L) and right (R) side. Pull the right clutch up (or push from the back) and, at the same time, push the left clutch down. The cylinder can now move freely. Move it down to access the coffee filter.
3. Place the brewer in vertical position with the brewer locking grip facing upwards.
4. Locate the 2 screws in between the gears. Loosen and remove the 2 screws. (3.5/Length=8mm)
5. Remove the old coffee filter.
6. Place the new coffee filter. ▪Make sure that the (coffee) water connectors are in line
with each other
▪When needed, turn the coffee filter slightly to fit the
square filter shaft into the drive gear.
7. Secure the coffee filter with 2 screws.
Install inner cylinder
Follow this procedure:
1. Place the brewer on a flat surface as shown in the picture. Push the cylinder against the coffee filter.
2. Lower the inner cylinder inside the brewer and tilt it around the piston.
3. Slide it inside the outer cylinder.
4. Turn the brewer upside down. Secure the inner cylinder with 1 screw (M4x16).
Install inlet filter
Follow this procedure:
1. Position the new inlet filter. ▪Align it with the transparent water coupling (inset 1).
▪Lower the filter on the bayonet locking (inset 2) and turn
the filter to lock.
▪Secure the inlet filter with 1 screw (3). (M4/
Length=16mm)
2. Finished, the service parts are installed.
3. Place the cover and install the brewer in the coffee machine.

components.title: Unlock the brewer
components.text:
In rare situations the brewer system can lock itself. If, for instance, the door of the coffee machine is opened during a coffee brewing cycle the brewer is halted for safety reasons and can remain in an unknown position.
1. Remove the brewer from the coffee machine.
2. Remove the cover.
3. Turn the gear (1) and check if the piston will move up and down (see arrows) on the two lead screw piston transports.
4. Install the brewer in the coffee machine and dispense a coffee.

components.title: Place brewer in service position
components.text:
To replace all serviceable parts, the inlet filter must be pulled out of the coffee chamber first. A service option in the Service Menu can help to do this. Check the section CoEx XL service position (on page 134) for details.
If the option is not available in the Service Menu, it needs to be done manually.
1. Open the door and remove the brewer from the coffee machine.
2. Hold the brewer upside down.
3. Turn the main gear (1) counter clockwise.
4. The piston with inlet filter will move to the lowest position.

components.title: Calibrate the brewer / water flow meter
components.text: The water flow meter (water counter) measures the amount of water and is calibrated in the factory. When the water flow meter is replaced, it needs to be calibrated once. The system needs to 'know' how much water is entering the brewer and how to position the needle in the flow regulator to make sure the amount of water is correct. Check the procedure in the Calibrations (on page 109) section for more details.

components.title: Mixer
components.text:
The mixer consists of a mixer motor, a mixer propeller and a mixer house. The mixer is controlled by the control board and ensures a correct mixing of the ingredient(s) and water. By the rotation of the mixer propeller, air is mixed with the water and ingredient(s) and a foam layer is formed. This will improve the taste and the appearance of the consumption.
Motor specification: 24VDC, 14.000 RPM. In case of a blockage, a safety is actuated on the IO board and the message “mixer blocked” is shown in the screen.
A restricted inlet diameter of the mixer house is used to create a nice flow in the mixer bowl.

components.title: Brewercyclus (CoEx XL)
components.text:
De CoEx XL-brewercyclus
Dit is één volledige cyclus van de CoEx XL-brewer.
1. De CoEx XL-brewer staat in de startpositie. De brewercilinder zit tegen de koffiefilter geklemd, zodat een brewerkamer ontstaat. De molen draait en de gemalen koffie valt vanuit de molenuitlaat in de brewerkamer (1).
2. Twee door een motor aangedreven transportspindels (1) bewegen de zuiger (2) heen en weer. Tijdens het malen wordt koffie dat in de brewerkamer valt richting het einde geduwd om morsen te voorkomen. Dit kan handig zijn als een dubbele dosering van gemalen koffie is geselecteerd.
3. Zodra de gewenste dosering is bereikt, stopt het malen. De zuiger (1) met daarbovenop de inlaatfilter (2) beweegt binnenin de cilinder. De gemalen koffie wordt tegen de roterende koffiefilter (3) geperst waardoor een koffiepuck (CP) ontstaat.
4. Heet water komt via een slangetje (1), dat is aangesloten op de inlaatfilter, in de brewer en wordt door de koffiepuck (CP), de koffiefilter (2) en de in de debietregelaar (3) geperst.
5. De naald (4) in de debietregelaar beweegt om het debiet te reguleren (druk en extractietijd).
6. Aan het einde van de brewercyclus gaat de naald in de positie ‘beluchten’ zodat de koffie-uitlaat leeg kan lopen.
7. De zuiger (1) beweegt naar achteren en koppelt met de brewercilinder door middel van de koppelingen (2) en (3) en trekt de brewercilinder weg van de koffiefilter.
8. De zuiger (1) beweegt opnieuw naar voren, ontkoppelt alle koppelingen en laat de brewercilinder in dezelfde positie staan. De gebruikte koffiepuck wordt uit de cilinder geperst.
De koffiepuckwisser (2) beweegt de koffie naar de afvalbak en verwijdert koffieresten van het oppervlak van de inlaatfilter.
9. De zuiger (1) beweegt helemaal naar voren en perst de brewercilinder (2) tegen het koffiefilter (3) waar het vast blijft zitten.
10. De naald (4) beweegt naar de “spoel"-positie om achtergebleven output naar de afvoeruitlaat te leiden.
11. De zuiger gaat terug naar de startpositie en is klaar voor de volgende uitgifte.
12. De naald in de debietregelaar gaat terug naar de startpositie.

components.title: CoEx XL brewer verwijderen en plaatsen
components.text:
Verwijderingsprocedure
Voer de volgende stappen uit om de brewer te verwijderen:
1. Plaats om de brewer uit de koffiemachine te verwijderen vier vingers in de onderste greep (1). Druk de grendel (2) in met uw duim en trek de brewer in de richting van de pijl uit het frame (3).
Plaatsingsprocedure
Voer de volgende stappen uit om de brewer te plaatsen:
1. Zorg ervoor dat de binnenkant van het brewerframe schoon is.
2. Plaats de brewer in het frame en duw hem in de vergrendelingen.
▪Alle andere koppelingen gaan automatisch.
▪De brewer initialiseert één keer wanneer de eerste koffie-
uitgifte is gestart. Alle breweronderdelen worden eerst in de juiste startpositie gezet.

components.title: Service-onderdelen van de brewer vervangen
components.text:
De enige onderdelen in de brewer die na 50.000 brewingcycli (of na 2 jaar) moeten worden vervangen zijn:
1. de koffiefilter met afdichtingen
2. de binnenste cilinder
3. de inlaatfilter met afdichtingen.
Er is een complete set aan reserveonderdelen verkrijgbaar.
Het serienummer van de CoEx XL (zichtbaar op een hitte- en waterbestendig label op de tandwielkast van de brewer) bevat de productiedatum. De getalnotatie is jaar-week-volgnummer.
Procedure
Volg de stappen voor het vervangen van service-onderdelen.
1. Zet de brewer voordat u deze uit de machine verwijdert eerst in de Service-positie. In het servicemenu is een optie die u daarbij kan helpen. Zie het hoofdstuk Brewer in service-positie plaatsen (op pagina 67).
2. Verwijder de brewer uit de machine en verwijder de kap van de brewer. Zie voor meer informatie het hoofdstuk ‘De brewer verwijderen en reinigen’ in de gebruikershandleiding.
Verwijder inlaatfilter
Volg deze procedure:
1. Verwijder één schroef (1) waarmee het inlaatfilter is bevestigd. (M4/Lengte=16mm)
2. Draai het inlaatfilter naar rechts (2) om de bayonetsluiting te openen.
3. Maak het inlaatfilter los en verwijder het van de zuiger.
Verwijder binnenste cilinder
Volg deze procedure:
1. Verwijder 1 schroef waarmee de binnenste cilinder is bevestigd. (M4/Lengte=16mm).
2. Draai de brewer weer om.
3. Schuif de binnenste cilinder (1) uit de buitenste cilinder. Kantel (2) hem en verwijder hem uit de brewer.
Vervang koffiefilter
Volg deze procedure:
1. Duw de cilinder met de hand naar beneden.
2. Als de cilinder is vergrendeld, zoek dan de koppelingen aan de linker- (L) en rechterkant (R). Duw de rechter koppeling omhoog (of duw vanaf de achterkant) en duw tegelijkertijd de linker koppeling naar beneden. De cilinder kan nu vrij bewegen. Beweeg hem naar beneden om bij de koffiefilter te kunnen.
3. Plaats de brewer in verticale positie, waarbij de vergrendeling van de brewer naar boven wijst.
4. Lokaliseer de 2 schroeven tussen de tandwielen. Draai de 2 schroeven los en verwijder ze. (3,5/Lengte=8mm)
5. Verwijder het oude koffiefilter.
6. Plaats de nieuwe koffiefilter. ▪Zorg ervoor dat de (koffie-) wateraansluitingen in lijn zijn
met elkaar.
▪Draai indien nodig het koffiefilter iets zodat de vierkante
filterhouder in het aandrijftandwiel past.
7. Bevestig het koffiefilter met 2 schroeven.
Installeer binnenste cilinder
Volg deze procedure:
1. Plaats de brewer op een vlakke ondergrond, zoals in de afbeelding weergegeven. Duw de cilinder tegen het koffiefilter.
2. Zet de binnenste cilinder in de brewer en kantel hem rond de zuiger.
3. Schuif hem in de buitenste cilinder.
4. Draai de brewer onderste boven. Bevestig de binnenste cilinder met 1 schroef (M4x16).
Installeer het inlaatfilter
Volg deze procedure:
1. Plaats het nieuwe inlaatfilter. ▪Lijn het uit met de transparante waterkoppeling (inzet 1).
▪Laat het filter op de bayonetsluiting zakken (inzet 2) en
draai het filter om te vergrendelen.
▪Bevestig het inlaatfilter met 1 schroef (3). (M4/
Lengte=16mm)
2. Klaar! De service-onderdelen zijn geïnstalleerd.
3. Plaats de kap en installeer de brewer in de koffiemachine.

components.title: Brewer ontgrendelen
components.text:
In zeldzame situaties kan het brewersysteem zichzelf vergrendelen. Bijvoorbeeld als de deur van de koffiemachine tijdens een koffiecyclus is geopend, wordt de brewer voor de veiligheid stopgezet en kan hij in een onbekende positie blijven staan.
1. Verwijder de brewer uit de koffiemachine.
2. Verwijder de kap.
3. Draai het tandwiel (1) en controleer of de zuiger op de twee zuigertransporten met spindel naar boven en beneden kan bewegen (zie pijlen).
4. Installeer de brewer in de koffiemachine en tap een koffie.

Als de optie in het servicemenu niet beschikbaar is, dan moet het handmatig worden uitgevoerd.
1. Open de deur en verwijder de brewer uit de koffiemachine.
2. Houd de brewer onderste boven.
3. Draai het hoofdtandwiel (1) tegen de klok in.
4. De zuiger met inlaatfilter beweegt naar de laagste positie.

components.title: Schaerer grinder
components.text:
By adjusting the upper grinder blade axially, the air gap between the two grinder blades can be set very accurately. This air gap defines the grain size of the ground coffee, what is known as the grinding degree. The grinding degree setting is made manually on a worm gear. The powder (ground coffee) is discharged into the powder outlet through four cams attached evenly around the circumference of the star shaft.

Changing the grinding degree
The grinder disc contains grinding degree numbers from 0 to 5.
The grinder is set to a default grinding degree of 1.5 (S=Standard model) or 2 (XG=XG model using advanced grinder discs) during production. However, the type of coffee beans used and (local) flavor expectations will probably be different. Adjust the grinding degree for the best ground coffee and ‘fine-tune’ for the best flavor coffee and espresso. The grinder needs to be removed from the machine to change the grinding degree. A fixation spring is used to secure the grinding disc to a specific grinding degree.
1. Remove the fixation spring. ▪Bend the teeth away from the grinding disc and lift the
spring.
2. Rotate the grinding disc to change the grinder degree. ▪Set it 0.5 lower for a finer grinding.
▪Set it 0.5 higher for a more coarse-grained coffee.
3. Insert the fixation spring.

components.title: Filterfresh brewing system
components.text:
1. Brewer chamber
2. Transport wheels
3. Brewer outlet
4. Piston
5. Cylinder
The brewer operates according to the vacuum principle.
Ground coffee is dosed into the brewer chamber, together with the hot water. At that moment the brewer is in the rest mode (A).
Then the brewer motor turns, moving the piston up (B). This movement mixes the water and the coffee mixed, improving the extraction. Consequently, less ground coffee is necessary to obtain stronger and more tasteful coffee. Subsequently, the piston moves down, pulling the coffee through the filter paper (C). The coffee flows out of the cylinder through the outlet into the cup. The filter paper together with the coffee residue is transported by means of the transport wheels, when the piston is in the almost lower position and the brewer chamber is lifted.
After this, the brewer returns to the rest mode (D) and is ready for the next cycle.

components.title: Brewer cycle (CoEx XL)
components.text:
The CoEx XL brewer cycle
This is one complete cycle of the CoEx XL brewer.
1. The CoEx XL brewer is in starting position. The brewer cylinder is locked against the coffee filter to create a brewer chamber.
The grinder runs and the ground coffee falls from the grinder outlet into the brewer chamber (1).
2. Two, motor powered, transport lead screws (1) move the piston (2) back and forth. During grinding, coffee dropped in the brewer chamber is pushed towards the end to prevent spillage. This can be useful when a double dosage of ground coffee is selected.
3. When the required dosage is reached, grinding stops. The piston (1), with on top the inlet filter (2) moves inside the cylinder. The ground coffee, is pressed against the rotating coffee filter (3) creating a coffee puck (CP).
4. Hot water is inserted in the brewer cylinder via a small hose (1) connected to the inlet filter and pressed through the coffee puck (CP), through the coffee filter (2) and into the flow regulator (3).
5. The needle (4) inside the flow regulator moves to regulate the flow (pressure and extraction time).
6. At the end of the brewing cycle, the needle is moved to the ‘aerate’ position to allow the coffee outlet to empty.
7. The piston (1) moves back and connects to the brewer cylinder using the clutches (2) and (3) and pulls the brewer cylinder away from the coffee filter.
8. The piston (1) moves forward again, disconnects all clutches and leaves the brewer cylinder in the same position. The used coffee puck is pushed out of the cylinder. The coffee puck wiper (2) moves the coffee to the waste bucket and cleans the surface of the inlet filter from coffee residue.
9. The piston (1) moves forward completely and pushes the brewing cylinder (2) against the coffee filter (3) where it remains locked.
10. The needle (4) moves to the ‘flush’ position to redirect any remaining output to the drain outlet.
11. The piston returns to the start position and is ready for the next brew.
12. The needle in the flow regulator returns to the starting position.

components.title: Brewercyclus
components.text:
Startpositie
Na dosering van de koffie wordt de brewer geactiveerd. De motor draait met de klok mee tot gesloten positie.
Gesloten positie
De gedoseerde koffie wordt tussen de boven- en onderzuiger samengeperst. Hierna wordt water via de zuiger door de samengeperste koffie geperst. Het stroomt vervolgens door het filter in de bovenkant en uitlaat van de brewer. De druk van de zuiger op de samengeperste koffie wordt geregeld door de regelbare stroom van de motor.
Open positie
Als er voldoende water is gedoseerd, draait de brewer tegen de klok in naar de open positie.
Restwisser
De brewer loopt door, waarbij de onderzuiger naar de bovenste positie beweegt. Nu draait de brewer met de klok mee en wordt de samengeperste koffie van de zuiger in de afvalbak geveegd.
Terug naar start
Nadat de koffieresten zijn weggeveegd, draait de brewer met de klok mee naar de startpositie.
Startpositie
De brewer is klaar voor een nieuwe cyclus.

components.title: Remove the brewer
components.text:
Required
Use the following parts to perform the procedure:
• Blue brewer key
• Green service key
Procedure
Perform the following steps:
1. Tear off the filter paper on the left and right of the brewer.
2. Insert the service key in the door.
3. In the Service menu tap the [Replace filter paper] button. ▪ The brewer chamber will move up to the open position.
4. Remove the service key from the door.
5. Remove the brewer chamber by pulling it in the direction of the arrow.
6. Remove the remaining old filter paper from the brewer. ▪ Lift the transport wheels with the cantilever if needed.
7. Remove the nozzle / outlet pipe from the brewer.
8. Take the brewer out of the machine. First tilt the lower part of the brewer towards you to release the main shaft from the motor interlocking.
▪ Tilting the lower part about 10 cm is enough.
9. Lift the brewer a little to release the studs from the suspension and remove the brewer from the coffee machine.

components.title: Clamp force adjustment
components.text:
Readjusting the clamp fore is necessary when too much water leaks between the brewer and the brewer chamber. This is the case when the filter paper becomes wet, more the 10 mm around the brewer chamber. Nevertheless, when the clamp force is adjusted to high, excessive wear can occur or the brewer motor can get stuck.
Adjust the brewer chamber clamp force as follows:
1. Open the machine door.
2. Tear the filter paper in front of the brewer and behind the brewer.
3. Remove the brewer from the machine.
4. Turn the brewer piston up using the Uni-key until the brewer chamber flips over.
5. Remove the filter paper from the brewer. Place a new piece of filter paper between the brewer and the brewer chamber.
6. Move the brewer piston in the upper position (connecting rods in line).
7. Turn the adjustment nut on top of the H-frame clockwise, until filter paper is just clamped between brewer and brewer chamber. The brewer chamber may not be pushed onto the brewer during the adjustment.
8. Turn the nut ½ - 1 turn clockwise.
9. Place the brewer in the machine
10. Place the filter paper according to the procedure in the user’s manual.
11. Check the operation of the brewer by selecting a coffee consumption.
Take notice of the following things: When the brewer chamber clamp force is set too low, water is leaking between the brewer and the brewer chamber. Turn the adjustment nut one quarter of a turn clockwise. The clamp force is set too high when the brewer piston does not move smoothly in the down position (during lifting of the brewer chamber). Turn the adjustment nut one quarter of a turn counter-clockwise. Check operation of the brewer again.
12. Close the machine door.

components.title: Removal and placement of the CoEx XL brewer
components.text:
Removal procedure
Perform the following steps to remove the brewer:
1. To remove the brewer from the coffee machine, place four fingers in the lower grip (1). With your thumb, push and hold down the locking grip (2) and pull the brewer from the mounting frame in the direction of the arrow (3).
Placement procedure
Perform the following steps to install the brewer:
1. Make sure the inside of the brewer mounting frame in the coffee machine is clean.
2. Insert the brewer into the mounting frame and push until it locks.

▪ The brewer will initialize once when the first coffee dispense is started. All brewer parts are moved to the correct starting position first.

De bovenzuiger is verwijderbaar via de grendel aan de bovenkant van de brewer.
1. Draai de knop naar rechts om de filterkop te verwijderen.
2. Op de brewer plaatsen: Plaats eerst de volledige bovenzuiger in de juiste positie, draai de knop daarna naar links.

components.title: Paper transport distance
components.text:
To prevent that old coffee remains in the brewer chamber, during the transportation of the filter paper, the distance between the layers of coffee residue can be adjusted. Especially for large dosing quantities of coffee this can be necessary. Nevertheless the distance between the layers should not be adjusted too big, to prevent unnecessary loss of paper (more often replacement of the paper reel).
The paper transport is adjusted correct when: After transport of the filter paper, no coffee remains in the brewer chamber. The distance between the layers of coffee residue is between 5 – 10 mm.
Adjust the paper transport as follows:
1. Hold the adjustment bolt and loosen the lock nut.
2. Turn the adjustment bolt counter-clockwise when coffee residue remains in the brewer chamber / Turn the adjustment bolt clockwise when the distance between the layers of coffee residue is too big.
3. Tighten the lock nut.
4. Check the operation of the paper transport.
5. Check the distance between the layers of coffee residue.
6. Place the service key in the door switch. The machine is switched on now.
7. Take at least 4x consumptions to test the paper transport distance.
8. Check the functioning of the machine by taking a test drink (coffee). Place a cup or a jug underneath the nozzle to collect the hot test drink.

components.title: Replace service parts in the brewer
components.text:
The only serviceable parts in the brewer that need to be replaced after 50.000 brewing cycles (or 2 years) are:
1. the coffee filter assembly with seals.
2. the inner cylinder.
3. the inlet filter assembly with seals.
A complete set is available as spare part set.
The CoEx XL serial number (visible on a heat- and water resistant label on top of the brewer gear box) contains the manufacturing date. The number format is year-week-sequence number.
Procedure
Follow the steps to replace the service parts.
1. Before removing the brewer from the machine, first place the brewer in the Service position. A service option in the Service Menu can help to do this, check the section Place brewer in service position (on page 66).
2. Remove the brewer from the machine and remove the cover from the brewer. Check the chapter 'Remove and clean the brewer' in the User manual for details.
Remove inlet filter
Follow this procedure:
1. Remove one screw (1) that secures the inlet filter. (M4/ Length=16mm)
2. Turn the inlet filter clockwise (2) to release the bayonet locking.
3. Loosen and remove the inlet filter from the piston.
Remove inner cylinder
Follow this procedure:
1. Remove 1 screw that secures the inner cylinder. (M4/ Length=16mm).
2. Turn the brewer around again.
3. Slide the inner cylinder (1) out of the outer cylinder. Tilt (2) and remove it from the brewer.
Replace coffee filter
Follow this procedure:
1. Push the cylinder down by hand.
2. If the cylinder is locked, locate the clutches on the left (L) and right (R) side. Pull the right clutch up (or push from the back) and, at the same time, push the left clutch down. The cylinder can now move freely. Move it down to access the coffee filter.
3. Place the brewer in vertical position with the brewer locking grip facing upwards.
4. Locate the 2 screws in between the gears. Loosen and remove the 2 screws. (3.5/Length=8mm)
5. Remove the old coffee filter.
6. Place the new coffee filter. ▪ Make sure that the (coffee) water connectors are in line with each other
▪ When needed, turn the coffee filter slightly to fit the square filter shaft into the drive gear.
7. Secure the coffee filter with 2 screws.
Install inner cylinder
Follow this procedure:
1. Place the brewer on a flat surface as shown in the picture. Push the cylinder against the coffee filter.
2. Lower the inner cylinder inside the brewer and tilt it around the piston.
3. Slide it inside the outer cylinder.
4. Turn the brewer upside down. Secure the inner cylinder with 1 screw (M4x16).
Install inlet filter
Follow this procedure:
1. Position the new inlet filter. ▪ Align it with the transparent water coupling (inset 1).
▪ Lower the filter on the bayonet locking (inset 2) and turn the filter to lock.
▪ Secure the inlet filter with 1 screw (3). (M4/ Length=16mm)
2. Finished, the service parts are installed.
3. Place the cover and install the brewer in the coffee machine.

components.title: Drukschakelaar voor koffie/espresso regelen
components.text:
Dankzij het unieke, gepatenteerde systeem kan de CoEx®-brewer met één systeem koffie en espresso zetten. De druk is voor koffie en espresso verschillend; koffie wordt met een druk van 3 - 4 bar bereid, espresso met een druk van 9 bar.
Het volume van een consumptie is eenvoudig te wijzigen in de software-instellingen van de machine.
De contactduur tussen het water en het koffiepoeder is een heel belangrijke factor in de prestatie van de brewer en is voor koffie en espresso nagenoeg hetzelfde. De optimale contactduur tussen water en koffie is 15 - 25 seconden.
Om deze waarde te bereiken moet het systeem een restrictor gebruiken. Door de combinatie van hogere druk, lagere volume en een gelijke koffiecontactduur moet de uitstroom van espresso veel kleiner zijn dan de uitstroom van koffie. In de volgende afbeeldingen wordt de oplossing voor het maken van deze twee dranken in één systeem weergegeven.
1. Koffietoevoer Wanneer gekozen is voor koffie is de toevoer in het begin laag en wordt de drukschakelaar niet geactiveerd. (Veer is sterk genoeg om de drukschakelaar in de koffiestand te houden).
De koffie passeert de eerste restrictor en stroomt dan door de grote koffie-uitlaat.
2. Espressotoevoer Wanner gekozen is voor espresso dan is de toevoer eerst hoog en wordt de drukschakelaar geactiveerd. (Veer is niet sterk genoeg om de drukschakelaar in de koffiestand te houden).
De koffie-uitlaat wordt gesloten en de espresso moet door de tweede restrictie worden geperst, waardoor de toevoer wordt beperkt en de druk naar 9 bar wordt verhoogd.
Het drukverschil tussen koffie en espresso is alleen van toepassing op B2C-espressomachines. De CoEx® Fresh Brew-machines (zonder papieren filter) hebben geen veer om tussen koffie- of espresso-druk te schakelen.
De bovenzuiger heeft een gekleurde stip die verwijst naar de gatmaat/-maten en drukschakelaar.

components.title: Remove the brewer chamber
components.text:
The brewer chamber needs to be removed weekly for cleaning. If the brewer is in the open position, the brewer chamber can be removed.
Make sure the pins are fixed correctly by placing the brewer chamber back.

components.title: Unlock the brewer
components.text:
In rare situations the brewer system can lock itself. If, for instance, the door of the coffee machine is opened during a coffee brewing cycle the brewer is halted for safety reasons and can remain in an unknown position.
1. Remove the brewer from the coffee machine.
2. Remove the cover.
3. Turn the gear (1) and check if the piston will move up and down (see arrows) on the two lead screw piston transports.
4. Install the brewer in the coffee machine and dispense a coffee.

components.title: Afdichtingen in onderzuiger vervangen
components.text:
Benodigd gereedschap
Schroevendraaier
Procedure
Voer de volgende stappen uit:
1. Draai de bout (1) van de brewer uit en draai de andere twee bouten (2) los.
2. Draai de onderste bouten (2) slechts 1,5 slag. Verwijder ze niet.
3. Trek de linker en rechter behuizing aan beide kanten van de cilinder (1) uit elkaar en trek de cilinder en de zuiger opwaarts uit de brewer (2).
4. Verwijder de zuiger uit de cilinder.
5. Vervang de onderdelen (zie volgend hoofdstuk) en installeer ze in omgekeerde volgorde.

components.title: Place brewer in service position
components.text:
To replace all serviceable parts, the inlet filter must be pulled out of the coffee chamber first. A service option in the Service Menu can help to do this. Check the section CoEx XL service position (on page 122) for details.
If the option is not available in the Service Menu, it needs to be done manually.
1. Open the door and remove the brewer from the coffee machine.
2. Hold the brewer upside down.
3. Turn the main gear (1) counter clockwise.
4. The piston with inlet filter will move to the lowest position.

components.title: Place brewer in service position
components.text:
To replace all serviceable parts, the inlet filter must be pulled out of the coffee chamber first. A service option in the Service Menu can help to do this. Check the section CoEx XL service position (on page 116) for details.
If the option is not available in the Service Menu, it needs to be done manually.
1. Open the door and remove the brewer from the coffee machine.
2. Hold the brewer upside down.
3. Turn the main gear (1) counter clockwise.
4. The piston with inlet filter will move to the lowest position.

components.title: Afdichtingen
components.text:
De brewer heeft twee zuigers; de bovenzuiger (beter bekend als filterkop) en de onderzuiger. Drie afdichtringen zijn verantwoordelijk voor het afdichten van de drukruimte: twee in de onderzuiger en één in de bovenzuiger.
1. Onderzuiger
2. Afdichtring (onderzuiger)
3. U-cupafdichtring - ROOD (onderzuiger)
4. U-cupafdichtring - BLAUW (bovenzuiger)
5. Bovenzuiger / filterkop
Heet water komt de cilinder binnen (via de onderzuiger) tussen de twee afdichtringen in de zuiger. De mix van water en koffiepoeder wordt door het gaas in de bovenzuiger gefilterd en verlaat vervolgens de cilinder. De afdichting in de bovenzuiger en de onderzuiger moeten tijdens het brewingproces bestand zijn tegen de druk van heet water (10 bar). De vorm van de u-cupring (3) voorkomt krassen in de cilinder door koffiekorrels. De bovenste afdichtring (2) hoeft niet bestand te zijn tegen hoge druk, maar is slechts een schraapring.

components.title: Calibrate the brewer / water flow meter
components.text: The water flow meter (water counter) measures the amount of water and is calibrated in the factory. When the water flow meter is replaced, it needs to be calibrated once. The system needs to 'know' how much water is entering the brewer and how to position the needle in the flow regulator to make sure the amount of water is correct. Check the procedure in the Calibrations (see Calibration of Water flow meter on page 125) section for more details.

components.title: Calibrate the brewer / water flow meter
components.text: The water flow meter (water counter) measures the amount of water and is calibrated in the factory. When the water flow meter is replaced, it needs to be calibrated once. Check the procedure in the Calibrations (see Calibration of Water flow meter on page 119) section for more details.

components.title: Replace the flow regulator
components.text:
Purpose
There is no need to replace the flow regulator. Regular cleaning of the machine will keep the flow regulator clean and working properly. Replace only if requested by the service department.
Required
Use the following parts to perform the procedure:
• Philips screwdriver
• Flow regulator replacement set with part number 9ZBR108.

components.title: Remove the flow regulator
components.text:
Procedure
1. Remove the CoEx XL brewer from the machine.
2. Remove the cover from the brewer.
3. Make sure the brewer is clean. ▪ Clean with warm water (a mild detergent may be added) and make sure to remove any leftover coffee grains.
4. Remove the screw (A) that secures the outlet support (C).
5. Loosen the flexible connections (B) and remove the outlet support.
6. Remove the two screws (A) from the flow regulator (B).
7. Lift the spindle end (A) from the brewer frame. ▪ If needed, rotate the spindle end first to release it from the brewer frame.
▪ Unlock the spindle gear (B) from the guide (C).
8. Slide and lift the flow regulator (D) from the regulator pipe (E) where it connects to the filter.
9. Pull the spindle gear (A) away from the flow regulator (B) until the needle (C) is visible.
10. Turn the spindle gear (A) 180° -in either direction- and unlock it from the needle (B).

components.title: Install a new flow regulator
components.text:
1. Use the new flow regulator (C) and connect the spindle gear (A) to the needle (B).
2. Turn the spindle gear (A) 180° -in either direction-to lock it to the needle (B).
3. Push the spindle gear (A) into the regulator (C) and check that the spindle gear is locked to the needle (B) as shown in the picture.
▪ Note that the needle locking is visible.
4. Pump the spindle gear in and out a few times to make sure the needle in the flow regulator can move freely.
5. Position the spindle gear (A) under the inlet water hose (B) first.
6. Insert the flow regulator (C) in the regulator pipe (D).
7. Insert the spindle end (E) in the frame at the back of the brewer.
▪ Rotate the spindle end, if needed, to adjust the length and fit it in the frame.
8. Push down the middle of the spindle gear (A) to lock it in the guide (F) inside the frame.
9. Secure the flow regulator (A) with two screws (B). ▪ Do not tighten the screws too hard.
10. Connect the two flexible connections (A) of the outlet support (B) to the flow regulator (C) and secure with one screw (D).
11. The replacement is finished.
12. Place the cover on the brewer and install the brewer in the machine.

components.title: Test the flow regulator
components.text:
1. Place the service key.
2. Login in the Service Menu.
3. Tap the [HARDWARE] button.
4. Make sure the waste bucket is completely dry. ▪ During execution of the test recipe in the next step, check for water in the waste bucket.
5. Tap the [Test espresso recipe] button. ▪ Check that:
a. no water leaks in the waste bucket during execution of the test recipe.
b. at the end of the recipe, the needle moves to the flush position and releases a small amount of water. This amount of water is visible in the waste bucket.

components.title: Grinder
components.text: The coffee machine can contain one or two grinders. They are mounted inside the machine on the canister plate.

components.title: Ingredient canisters (Instant Medium / Instant Small)
components.text:
The canisters are provided with a metal or plastic auger. The metal auger is used for instant coffee, instant tea and leaf tea.
The plastic auger is used for the other ingredients. Special augers are available for special ingredients or low gram throws.
All canisters are driven by a 24VDC 120RPM motor.

components.title: General
components.text:
The D-grinder uses high performance grinder discs that give a consistent grind and operates at about twice the speed of the Schaerer grinder to grind beans for coffee and espresso. This means that the same amount of ground coffee is created in half the time. Check the specifications at the end of this chapter for more details. The D-grinder is easy to clean and settings (like grinding degree) are maintained when the grinder is opened for cleaning. The grinding degree of the D-grinder is not measured in pins and teeth but displayed in an indicator window on the grinder. The indicator shows a scale from 0 to 12 (actual degrees divided by 10). The D-grinder is set to a default grinding degree of 6 in the factory. Note that the type of beans used and (local) flavor expectations may require a different setting of the grinder in the coffee machine.
1. Auger 10. Grinder motor drive
2. Grinder house top assembly 11. Grinding degree adjustment screw
3. Upper grinding disc (stationary) 12. Grinding degree scale window
4. Screws upper grinding disc 13. Grinder adjustment cover
5. Screws lower grinding disc 14. Screws worm wheel assembly
6. Lower grinding disc (rotating) 15. Adjustment wheel
7. Grinder base / Motor cover 16. Grinder outlet
8. Grinder stand 17. Drive shaft
9. Grinder house 18. Grinding disc assembly bottom
The grinder unit consists of the top assembly (2) that contains the stationary –non moving-upper grinding disc (3). The top assembly is secured to the grinder house using a bayonet catch for easy access. The grinder house (9) contains the bottom assembly with the rotating lower grinding disc (6). By adjusting the lower grinding disc up and down, the air gap between the two grinder discs can be set very accurately. The gap between the two grinder discs determines the grain size of the ground coffee also known as the grinding degree. The grinding degree is set manually by rotating the adjustment wheel (15) with an adjustment screw (11). This screw is accessible when the grinder is installed in the coffee machine. The adjustment wheel contains a grinding degree scale that is visible through a small window (12). A 24-volt motor in the grinder base powers the lower grinding disc via a gear box to the drive shaft (17).

components.title: Change the grinding degree
components.text:
The grinding degree can be adjusted without removing the grinder from the coffee machine.
The actual grinding degree is visible in a small indicator window in the bottom left of the grinder.
1. Adjust the grinding degree with the (Philips type) screw, accessible on the bottom right of the grinder base.
▪ Turn left (+) for a coarser grinding / higher number.
▪ Turn right (-) for a finer grinding / lower number.
▪ Turn the screw in the desired direction and check the indicator to see the current grinding degree.
Set the grinding degree to the value 6 (factory default) or to the preferred value that was already known.
Take a test beverage to test for taste and write down the finally set grinding degree for future reference.
The outer areas of the scale are marked in red (values lower than 1.5 and higher than 10.5).
This is only needed once (or when installing a new grinder or new grinder discs).

components.title: Remove and place the grinder
components.text:
1. To access the grinder, first remove the bean canister. ▪ The grinder is placed and positioned on grinder stands inside the grinder base and is secured only using the driving shaft.
2. To remove the grinder, lift it from the grinder base in the direction of the arrow.
3. Place the grinder in the grinder base and make sure the grinder outlet points in the right direction.
▪ Rotate the grinder auger to allow the drive shaft to ‘fit’ and move down completely. The drive shaft must ‘fit’ in the motor drive.

components.title: Clean the grinder
components.text:
Regular (monthly) cleaning of the grinder is recommended to prevent clogging of old ground coffee inside the grinder house.
Also, burned beans and ‘foreign’ objects (like wood or stones) can block the grinder and need to be removed.
Procedure
Perform the following steps:
1. Remove the grinder from the machine.
2. Open the grinder house.
3. Clean the grinder discs and the inside of the grinder house (do not forget to clean the gap around the discs).
4. Close the grinder house.
5. Install the grinder in the machine.

components.title: Replace the grinder discs
components.text:
The upper and lower discs are identical.
The screws in the lower and the upper disc are NOT identical.
Required tools
• Philips screwdriver
Procedure
Perform the following steps:
1. Remove the grinder from the machine.
2. Remove the grinder outlet. ▪ spread the two fixation clips (1) that secure the outlet to the grinder.
▪ slide the outlet in the direction of the arrow (2) and remove it from the grinder.
3. Remove the grinder house top assembly. ▪ Turn the cover of the top assembly in the direction of the arrow (clockwise!) to unlock the bayonet catch and remove the top assembly from the grinder.
4. Remove screws from upper grinding disc.
5. Remove the upper disc.
6. Before placing the new upper grinding disc make sure that the mounting surface is clean.
7. Place the upper grinder disc.
8. Secure the upper disc with three screws.
Tighten the screws gently, but firmly.
9. Loosen and remove the three screws in the lower disc.
10. Remove the lower disc.
11. Clean up the grinder house and make sure that the mounting surface for the lower grinding disc is clean (to prevent a different grinding degree).
12. Place the new lower grinding disc.
13. Secure the lower grinding disc with three screws.
Tighten the screws gently, but firmly.
14. Close the grinder house. ▪ Install grinder house top assembly.
▪ Place the grinder house top assembly on top of the grinder and turn it in the direction of the arrow (counter clockwise!) to close and lock it to the grinder house.
15. Install grinder outlet. ▪ Slide the grinder outlet in the direction of the arrow on the outside of the grinder house and make sure the locking clips of the outlet lock properly.

components.title: Readjust the D-grinder (CoEx Medium)
components.text:
The D-grinder has been set in the factory to the default grinding degree of 6, this number corresponds to a gap between the two grinder discs of about 0.25 mm.
Readjustment is possible if this number, shown in the little window on the grinder, does not match with the actual gap between the grinder discs. This can happen :
• when new grinder discs are installed.
• after the initial break-in period of the grinder discs (after grinding beans for 1000 cups of coffee).
Required tools
• Torx 20 screwdriver
Procedure
Perform the following steps
1. Remove the adjustment cover. ▪ Bend the four locking clips (1) in the direction of the arrows and pull the adjustment cover (2) from the grinder house.
2. Remove the screws that secure the adjustment wheel. ▪ Pull the adjustment wheel from the drive shaft in the direction of the arrow. The adjustment disc is now visible.
3. To be able to turn the adjustment disc, insert two screws and give them a few turns.
4. Turn the adjustment disc gently in the direction of the arrow until the two grinding discs touch each other.
5. Check that the drive shaft cannot be turned anymore. ▪ The grinder discs are now reset to 0 (zero).
6. Remove the two support screws from the adjustment disc. ▪ Make sure not to change the current position of the adjustment disc.
7. Slide the adjustment wheel onto the drive shaft. The adjustment wheel contains a restrictor (1) that fits in a slot on the outside of the grinder house (2). The restriction slot limits the rotation of the adjustment wheel to 120º.
▪ Push the adjustment wheel down the shaft and turn it clockwise until the restrictor is in the left corner of the slot of the grinder house.
8. A second check: make sure that the number 0 of the scale on the adjustment wheel is positioned above the small vertical mark in the outside of the grinder house near the grinder outlet.
9. Secure the adjustment wheel with three screws. ▪ Tighten the screws gently but firmly.
10. Place the cover. The numbers 1 and 2 are embossed on the bottom outside of the adjustment cover. Position the number 1 in line with the grinder outlet. Position the number 2 in line with the grinder outlet for a grinder in door only.
▪ Slide the adjustment cover in the direction of the arrows and make sure that the four clips lock properly to the ledges on the outside of the grinder house.
11. The readjustment is now finished. Continue with the section Grinding degree (see Change the grinding degree on page 70) to set the grinder to the preferred grinding degree that was already noted down.

6. Remove the two support screws from the adjustment disc. ▪ Make sure not to change the current position of the adjustment disc.
7. Slide the adjustment wheel onto the drive shaft. The adjustment wheel contains a restrictor (1) that fits in a slot on the outside of the grinder house (2). The restriction slot limits the rotation of the adjustment wheel to 120º.
▪ Push the adjustment wheel down the shaft and turn it clockwise until the restrictor is in the left corner of the slot of the grinder house.
8. A second check: make sure that the number 0 of the scale on the adjustment wheel is positioned above the small vertical mark in the outside of the grinder house near the grinder outlet.
9. Secure the adjustment wheel with three screws. ▪ Tighten the screws gently but firmly.
10. Place the cover. The numbers 1 and 2 are embossed on the bottom outside of the adjustment cover. Position the number 1 in line with the grinder outlet. Position the number 2 in line with the grinder outlet for a grinder in door only.
▪ Slide the adjustment cover in the direction of the arrows and make sure that the four clips lock properly to the ledges on the outside of the grinder house.
11. The readjustment is now finished. Continue with the section Grinding degree (see Change the grinding degree on page 49) to set the grinder to the preferred grinding degree that was already noted down.

components.title: Readjust the D-grinder (CoEx XL Medium)
components.text:
The D-grinder has been set in the factory to the default grinding degree of 6, this number corresponds to a gap between the two grinder discs of about 0.25 mm.
Readjustment is possible if this number, shown in the little window on the grinder, does not match with the actual gap between the grinder discs. This can happen :
• when new grinder discs are installed.
• after the initial break-in period of the grinder discs (after grinding beans for 1000 cups of coffee).
Required tools
• Torx 20 screwdriver
Procedure
Perform the following steps
1. Remove the adjustment cover. ▪ Bend the four locking clips (1) in the direction of the arrows and pull the adjustment cover (2) from the grinder house.
2. Remove the screws that secure the adjustment wheel. ▪ Pull the adjustment wheel from the drive shaft in the direction of the arrow. The adjustment disc is now visible.
3. To be able to turn the adjustment disc, insert two screws and give them a few turns.
4. Turn the adjustment disc gently in the direction of the arrow until the two grinding discs touch each other.
5. Check that the drive shaft cannot be turned anymore. ▪ The grinder discs are now reset to 0 (zero).

7. Slide the adjustment wheel onto the drive shaft. The adjustment wheel contains a restrictor (1) that fits in a slot on the outside of the grinder house (2). The restriction slot limits the rotation of the adjustment wheel to 120º.

10. Place the cover. The numbers 1 and 2 are embossed on the bottom outside of the adjustment cover. Position the number 1 in line with the grinder outlet. Position the number 2 in line with the grinder outlet for a grinder in door only.

components.title: Mixer (CoEx Medium)
components.text:
The mixer consists of a mixer motor, a mixer propeller and a mixer house. The mixer is controlled by the control board and ensures a correct mixing of the ingredient(s) and water. By the rotation of the mixer propeller, air is mixed with the water and ingredient(s) and a foam layer is formed. This will improve the taste and the appearance of the consumption.
Motor specification: 24VDC, 14.000 RPM. In case of a blockage, a safety is actuated on the IO board and the message “mixer blocked” is shown in the screen.
A restricted inlet diameter of the mixer house is used to create a nice flow in the mixer bowl.

components.title: Canister plate beans canister
components.text:
Remove the canister plate bean canister
Perform the following steps:
1. Pull the canister lock in the direction of the arrow to release the bean canister from the grinder base.
2. Lift the canister from the grinder base and out of the coffee machine.
3. Install the bean canister - Place the bean canister on the grinder base and push the canister lock in the direction of the arrow.

components.text: Depending on the model, the coffee machine can contain coffee bean canisters on the canister plate or inside the door.

components.title: Ingredient canisters
components.text:
The canisters are provided with a metal or plastic auger. The metal auger is used for instant coffee, instant tea and leaf tea.
The plastic auger is used for the other ingredients. Special augers are available for special ingredients or low gram throws.
All canisters are driven by a 24VDC 120RPM motor.

components.title: Bekersensor (CoEx Medium)
components.text:
De bekersensor detecteert een beker op het bekerplateau. Er kunnen maximaal twee bekersensoren op de machine worden aangesloten. Een voor de rechter en een voor de linker uitlaat.
Een beker moet op de juiste positie op het bekerplateau worden geplaatst voordat de startknop beschikbaar is en de cyclus kan beginnen. De gevoeligheid van de sensor is in te stellen via het servicemenu, zie Bekersensor (op pagina 112).
PCB bekersensor (alle kleine en medium modellen)
De sensorbehuizing kan, afhankelijk van het machinetype, variëren. Zie voor meer informatie de handleidingen voor reserveonderdelen.

components.title: Bekersensor (CoEx XL Small)
components.text:
De bekersensor detecteert een beker op het bekerplateau. Er kunnen maximaal twee bekersensoren op de machine worden aangesloten. Een voor de rechter en een voor de linker uitlaat.
Een beker moet op de juiste positie op het bekerplateau worden geplaatst voordat de startknop beschikbaar is en de cyclus kan beginnen. De gevoeligheid van de sensor is in te stellen via het servicemenu, zie Bekersensor (op pagina 106).
PCB bekersensor (alle kleine en medium modellen)
De sensorbehuizing kan, afhankelijk van het machinetype, variëren. Zie voor meer informatie de handleidingen voor reserveonderdelen.

components.title: Cup sensor
components.text:
The cup sensor senses a cup on the cup stand. One PCB, containing two cup sensors, is connected in the machine. One for the left and one for the center outlet.
A cup must be placed on the correct position on the cup stand before the start button is available and the cycle can start. The sensitivity of the sensor is adjustable in the Service Menu section Cup sensor (on page 117) settings.
Cup sensor PCB (Nio models)
For further details, check the spare parts manual.

menu.title: Daily rinse / Daily cleaning cycle
menu.text: The rinse cycle needs to be done at least once a day. Place a jug or bin under the outlet nozzles before starting the rinse cycle. Check the User manual for more details. NOTE - This option can be disabled in the Service Menu Login > Filling & Cleaning > Filling & Cleaning > Cleaning Settings (not recommended and only if an alternative procedure is used as a daily cleaning procedure).

menu.title: Brewer cleaning cycle
menu.text: The brewer cleaning cycle needs to be done at least once a week. Tapping the brewer cleaning button will show a new screen with instructions. Follow the instructions and finish the whole procedure to reset the cleaning counter. If a "cleaning error" message appears, run the cleaning cycle again. Check the User manual for more details.
notes: Always complete the entire brewer cleaning cycle. If the cleaning cycle is interrupted, for instance by pressing the [CANCEL] button, the cleaning cycle must be repeated in full.
This option can be disabled in the section Login > Filling & Cleaning > Filling & Cleaning > Cleaning Settings (not recommended and only if an alternative procedure is used for this function).

menu.title: Functions with password (CoEx XL Medium / CoEx XL Small)
menu.text: Service mode password access After opening the door, the first level service screen is shown. To access the other service functions, login is needed. Tap the [Login] button to display the login screen. Enter the correct code and tap the [Login] button. Some options are only available / visible on the highest level (Level 4). 1. Input indicator 2. [Backspace] button 3. Numeric keypad with [0..9] buttons 4. [Login] button 5. [Back] button Service menu (After log in) In the Service menu a number of options are available to change the settings of your machine configuration. 1. Login Status 2. [Machine Information] button 3. Menu name 4. [Filling & Cleaning] button 5. [Hardware] button 6. [Installation] button 7. [Software] button 8. [Products] button 9. [Presentation] button 10. [Messages] button 11. [Exit] button All possible menu options are explained in the next sections. Functions available without a password (shown as soon as the door is opened) are listed in the previous sections. Several new buttons are introduced for specific actions. From top to bottom: • [Enable/Disable] button - acts as a slide switch, shown in disabled position. Swipe right or tap to enable (the switch will color to indicate that). • [Pencil] button - to change the contents of the field. • [Reset] button - to update or reset the value (e.g. set the date to today).

menu.title: Menu Layouts
menu.text: Login > Presentation > Vending menu layout / Jug menu layout This menu contains information and settings for the menu items, images and videos displayed on the screen of the coffee machine. Menu Layouts The menu items can be altered. First select the layout that needs to be changed: • [Vending (Cups) Menu Layout] • [Jug Menu Layout] To change the order of the menu items on the user screen, press and hold the [image] and drag the image to the new location. • If more than one category is configured, first tap the correct [category] button. • Swipe up and down to scroll to see all menu items. To see and change the (translated) names and image of the menu item: 1. Tap the [pencil] button in the desired menu item: ▪ To change the (translated) menu item name, tap the [pencil] button of the menu item. ▪ To change the image of the menu item, tap the [<] or [>] button and browse to the desired menu item image. 2. Tap the [Back] button to exit. ▪ Changes are saved immediately.

menu.title: Media
menu.text: Login > Presentation > Standby / Distributing / Logo / Background Images General • With the exception of the background and the info panel images, all other images can be handled remotely using ConnectMe. A valid ConnectMe account is needed. • Uploading videos to the coffee machine is only possible using ConnectMe. Video specifications Maximum video file size 300 Mb Supported formats mp4, mov, wmv, avi, qt, asf, x-msvideo, x-ms-wmv Image specifications Avy Maximum image file size 1 Mb Allowed image formats .png / .jpg / .gif (static) Display resolution 1920 x 1080 Image resolutions: • Standby images • 1920 x 1080 • Distributing images • 1200 x 671 • Logo image • 200 x 70 • Info panel image • 1200 x 700 • Background image • 1920 x 1080 For each image type, the following functions are available: • Tap the [Load <media> from USB] button to load one or more images from a USB stick, inserted in the USB port of the machine. • Tap the [Trash] button to remove an image from the machine. • To change the sequence of images shown on screen, press and hold the [image] button, then drag the item to the new position. • Tap the [Enable/Disable] switch to determine of the specific image will be shown or not. • Tap the [clock] button to change the display time (in seconds) of this specific image. Logo If the Logo image resolutions are specified in the table above, a user logo can be displayed on the screen. • Tap the [Select active logo] switch to select a logo if more than one logo is available on the machine. ▪ Only one logo can be shown at the same time. Standby media Standby images are displayed on the screen if the coffee machine is not used (is a screensaver). Standby after time delay time after the last dispensed beverage and the display of the first standby image. • Tap the [pencil] button to adjust the time. • Standby images are not shown when disabled. Show only touchless QR as standby images when enabled, a QR code is shown. A smartphone can be used for selection of a drink. Video volume tap the slider to adjust the volume of the standby video -- optional. Distributing media Distributing images are displayed during the preparation and dispense of the selected beverage. Video volume tap the slider to adjust the volume of the distributing video -- optional. Images can be connected to all consumptions (generic) or to specific products / recipes. 1. Select the generic or specific product. 2. Tap the [V] button for details. 3. Tap the [Add image] button to load one or more distributing images for the (generic) product. Info panel image If the Info images resolutions are specified in the table above an information image can be displayed when tapping the [Info] button on the main menu of the coffee machine. The info panel is language dependant. • First, tap the required [Language] button and then load the image from the USB stick. Background image The default background image can be changed. • Tap the desired [Select active background] switch to select one active background image (if more images are available).

menu.title: Touchless Interface
menu.text: Login > Presentation > Touchless Instead of using the touchscreen to select a drink, the screen displays a QR code that can be scanned by a smartphone. The code will direct the user to a web page with a selection of the drinks available on that machine. After placing a cup and selection of the desired drink on the smartphone, the machine will prepare the drink as usual. Touchless enabled tap the [switch] to enable the Touchless Interface. A machine specific QR code is displayed on the main menu. When enabled, the following options are also available: Show only touchless QR as standby image tap the [switch] to show the QR code instead of standby images if the machine is not used. Save printable QR to USB to save a QR code image. First, insert a USB stick in the USB port of the machine and then tap the [Save] button to store the image on the USB stick.
notes: The machine needs to be connected to the internet to use this functionality.

menu.title: Brewer cleaning cycle
menu.text: Main menu > Maintenance > Brewer Cleaning cycle The weekly cleaning cycle needs to be done at least 1x weekly. Pressing the weekly cleaning button will show a new screen with instructions. Follow the instructions and finish the whole procedure to reset the cleaning counter. If a cleaning error message appears, run the cleaning cycle again. Check the User manual for more details.
menu.path: Main menu > Maintenance > Brewer Cleaning cycle
notes: Always complete the entire brewer cleaning cycle. If the cleaning cycle is interrupted, for instance by pressing the [CANCEL] button, the cleaning cycle must be repeated in full.

menu.title: Reinigingscyclus brewer
menu.text: Hoofdmenu -> Onderhoud -> Reinigingscyclus brewer De wekelijkse reinigingscyclus moet minimaal 1x per week worden uitgevoerd. Door op de knop voor wekelijkse reiniging te drukken, wordt een nieuw scherm met instructies weergegeven. Volg de instructies en doorloop de hele procedure om de reinigingsteller te resetten. Als een melding van een reinigingsfout verschijnt, voert u de reinigingscyclus opnieuw uit. Zie de gebruikershandleiding voor meer informatie.
notes: Doorloop altijd de volledige reinigingscyclus van de brewer. Als de reinigingscyclus wordt onderbroken, bijvoorbeeld door op [ANNULEREN] te drukken, dan moet de reinigingscyclus in zijn geheel worden herhaald.

menu.title: Cleaning settings
menu.text: Login > Filling & Cleaning This menu contains information and settings (depending on model, type of configuration and login level) for the available cleaning messages. A message is displayed as a warning when the set time specified in the warning interval has expired. The machine will continue to work. If the time set in the critical interval has expired, the message is displayed and the machine is disabled completely. Cleaning error If a cleaning error message is displayed, tap the [Reset] button. The machine beeps, and the brewer cleaning message is cleared from the screen. Daily rinse [Enable/disable] switch - when disabled, the "Daily rinse needed" message is never displayed and the button is not available on the Filling & Cleaning menu (not recommended). When enabled, the following settings are available: Last executed shows date and time of the last daily rinse operation. Tap the [Reset] button to set it to the current date and time. • The daily cleaning procedure also resets this counter. Critical interval the message is displayed as an error after this number of hours has passed since the last daily rinse (default: 36). Brewer cleaning [Enable/disable] switch - when disabled, the "Rinse brewer with tablet" message is never displayed and the button is not available on the Filling & Cleaning menu (not recommended). When enabled, the following settings are available: Last executed shows date and time of the last brewer cleaning. Tap the [Reset] button to set it to the current date and time. • A brewer cleaning cycle resets this counter. Critical interval the message is displayed as an error after this number of hours has passed since the last brewer cleaning (default: 216). Waste bin fill level monitoring [Enable/disable] switch - when disabled, the "Waste bin full / Empty waste bin" message is never displayed. The button is not available on the Filling & Cleaning menu (not recommended). Reset when waste bin is removed for more than 4 seconds. When enabled, the waste bin switch is monitored. When the bin is removed for more than 4 seconds, the fill level is reset to zero. Current fill weight displays the calculated current filling level based on each coffee related dispense. Tap the [Reset] button to set the fill weight to zero. Critical level when the fill weight is more than this value, an error message is displayed. Tap the [pencil] button to change this level.

menu.title: Canister settings
menu.text: Login > Filling & Cleaning > Fill level monitoring The coffee machine can show a message "Canister x almost empty" when the canister contents are running low. After calibrating once, the coffee machine knows the starting weight of the ingredient in the canister and the amount that is dispensed with every recipe. The machine calculates the available amount after every dispense and displays the message if the predefined percentage levels are reached. Fill level monitoring The message can be enabled/disabled for each canister. Track Fill Level tap the [switch] to enable the desired canister: • [green] = fill level monitored • [grey] = fill level not monitored Full weight shows the weight of the completely filled ingredient canister. • Tap the [pencil] button to adjust the full weight. Almost empty warning percentage filling level when the message "Canister x almost empty" is displayed. • Tap the [pencil] button to adjust the percentage. In the Service Menu, check the section Login > Hardware > Calibrations > Ingredient Canister for the actual calibrations.

[grey] = fill level not monitored Full weight shows the weight of the completely filled ingredient canister.

menu.title: Cup sensors
menu.text: Login > Hardware > Cup sensors Cup sensor signal The signal of the sensors are read individually. This way the presence and visibility of a cup can be tested too. Cup sensor setting Tap the [Enable/Disable] switch to disable the sensor. When disabled, the machine works like there is no sensor. The sensitivity of the cup sensor is adjustable. The value can be adjusted between 0 and 4096. A higher value means less sensitive. So for detecting a transparent or dark colored cup the value must be set low. Measured shows the current measured value. Threshold value needed to trigger a cup present level. The message 'Place cup xxxx' is displayed (where xxxx will be left, right or middle) if this level is not reached. The default value is 100. This value gives the best detection for the most cup types. If there are two cup sensors in the machine, both are individually adjustable. Tap the [pencil] button to change the threshold value. Sensor 1 = Middle sensor. Sensor 2 = Right hand side sensor, hot (and cold -- optional) water.
notes: When disabled, drinks will be dispensed, even when no cup is placed.
Black cups or clear glass cups are not detectable, we advise to switch off the sensors if black cups or clear glass cups are used.

menu.title: Boiler(s) — CoEx Medium
menu.text: Current temperature Change temperature setting Login > Hardware > Boilers Shows the set and the actual temperature of the boiler(s) in degrees Celcius. Tap the [pencil] button to adjust the setting of the boiler. Recommended boiler temperature settings: Boiler Temperature Boiler 1 (pressure) 92 °C Boiler 2 (open) 91 °C The optimal temperature setting of the pressure boiler is 92 ºC. If no consumptions are made, the temperature in the boiler will automatically rise by 6 ºC in about 25 minutes. The first consumption with a cold brewer is now brewed with incoming water on a higher temperature, compensating the colder brewer.
notes: Sorte kopper eller klare glaskopper kan ikke detekteres, og vi anbefaler at slukke sensorerne, hvis der anvendes sorte kopper eller klare glaskopper.

menu.title: Calibration of canisters (CoEx Medium)
menu.text: Login > Hardware > Calibrations > Ingredient Canisters Calibrate Ingredient canisters Perform the following steps: 1. Fill up the ingredient canister as usual. 2. Weigh the complete filled canister. 3. Tap the Full weight [pencil] button of the desired ingredient canister and enter the weight. 4. If needed, tap the Almost empty warning [pencil] button to adjust the percentage (filling level) when the Canister almost empty message should be displayed. 5. Go back to the main menu and select the Hardware > Calibrations screen. 6. Select the desired ingredient canister and tap the [Calibrate] button. 7. Follow the steps on the screen and explained below. 8. Place a cup under the canister outlet and tap the [Next] button. ▪ The product motor runs for 3 seconds (just to fill up the outlets). ▪ Empty the cup. ▪ The second screen is shown. 9. Place a clean, empty cup on a scale and set the scale to 0 using the ‘tare’ function. 10. Place the empty cup under the canister outlet and tap the [Next] button again. ▪ The product motor runs for 10 seconds at full speed. 11. Weigh the amount of ingredient in the cup. 12. Enter the weight of the cup contents in the field and empty the cup. ▪ Tap [Retry] to repeat the previous action. ▪ Tap [Next] to continue with the next step. 13. Place the empty cup under the canister outlet and tap the [Next] button again. ▪ The product motor runs for 10 seconds at 80% speed. 14. Weigh the amount of ingredient in the cup. 15. Enter the weight of the cup contents in the field. ▪ Tap [Retry] to repeat the previous action. ▪ Tap [Next] to continue with the next step. 16. Check the entered details and tap [Save] when correct. ▪ Tap [Restart] to repeat the full procedure for this canister. 17. The procedure is now finished. ▪ Repeat the Calibrate procedure for another canister. After calibration, the canister needs to be activated for monitoring. Check the section Login > Filling & Cleaning > Filling & Cleaning > Canister Settings for more details.

menu.title: Calibration of Water flow meter (CoEx Medium)
menu.text: Login > Hardware > Calibrations > Water flow meter When the pressure reducer or water flow meter is replaced, the water flow meter (water counter) needs to be calibrated. Follow the steps below. 1. Open and close the door of the coffee machine to display the service menu. 2. Tap the [Daily rinse] button to rinse the hoses/boilers and remove air from the system. 3. Login with the highest level. 4. Allow the boilers to heat up and make sure the ”Wait, Heating boiler” message is removed from the screen. 5. Adjust the pressure reducer with an espresso recipe. ▪ This is only needed if the pressure reducer was replaced. Check the Pressure reducer section for more details. 6. From the list with components, search for the Flow meter entry and tap the [Calibrate] button. ▪ The procedure steps to calibrate the water flow meter are shown on the screen and explained below. 7. Place a clean, empty cup on a scale and set the scale to 0 using the ‘tare’ function. ▪ or use a measuring cup. 8. Open the door of the machine. 9. Place the cup below the waste water outlets inside the machine. 10. Tap the [Next] button. ▪ Insert the service key in the door to enable the button. 11. The cup is filled with water. ▪ when finished, the 2nd part of the menu is displayed. 12. Measure the amount of water in the cup. 13. Tap the [Next] button and enter the amount in the field on the screen. The amount should be about 125 ml. ▪ if the actual amount differs more than 5 ml, tap [Retry] to repeat the calibration step. 14. Tap the [Save] button to save the current value and finish the Calibration. 15. Leave the service menu and return to the main menu of the coffee machine. 16. Test a hot water dispense and check if the amount is the same as specified in the hot water recipe.
menu.path: Login > Hardware > Calibrations > Water flow meter

or use a measuring cup.

Show warning Shows the percentage of the total capacity of water that can be dispensed before a warning message is displayed. Capacity used (liters) Shows the total amount of water dispensed in drinks and during rinse procedures since the activation. Total lifetime Shows the number of days, after the installation date, that the water filter can be used. Show warning Shows the number of days after installation or activation before a warning message is displayed. Lifetime used Shows the number of days since the activation or replacement. Replace water filter Tap this button when the water filter is replaced. The water filter counters are reset.

menu.title: Empty open boiler
menu.text: In case the machine needs to be stored for a longer time, or needs to be transported (freezing weather, plane) the internal hoses and boilers needs to be emptied. The boilers are emptied due to gravity. Procedure Perform the following steps: 1. Remove the power cord from the wall socket. 2. Remove the cover on the back side of the machine. 3. Locate the grey hose with plug and the cut off clamp at the back of the machine. 4. Remove the plug at the end of the hose. ▪ Hold the end of the hose in a bucket or container (>5L). 5. Loosen the hose cut off clamp carefully. ▪ Potentially hot water will be drained out of the boiler. ▪ Wait until the boiler is empty. 6. Release the hose cut off clamp and place the plug in the hose.

menu.title: Empty pressure boilers (CoEx Medium)
menu.text: Login > Hardware > Drain boilers In case the machine needs to be stored for a longer time, or needs to be transported (freezing weather, plane) the internal hoses and boilers need to be emptied. The boilers are emptied due to gravity. Procedure Perform the following steps: 1. Switch off the machine and remove the power cord from the wall socket. 2. Close the connection to the water supply. 3. Remove the back cover plate from the machine. 4. Remove the plug from the metal elbow or T coupling right after the pump(s). See inset. 5. Connect a 6 mm hose to the elbow. ▪ Make sure the outlet of this hose ends in a large bucket, placed lower than the inlet valve of the machine. 6. Put the power cord back in the wall socket and switch the machine on. 7. Login in the service menu and tap [Hardware] > [Drain Boilers] > [Start]. 8. The procedure is now shown on the screen. 9. Place the service key and tap [Next] to start the draining process. ▪ The pumps will run for a short time, the 3-way valve opens to add air to the system. Slowly all water runs out of the boiler and hoses.

menu.title: Software
menu.text: Login > Software Active configuration Shows the currently active configuration. Other configurations Shows all other configurations on this machine. Delete Delete a configuration file. Backup Tap the [Backup] button of the desired configuration file to create a backup copy. A copy of the configuration file with all settings is made. The back-up file name is the original name and an added timestamp (year, month, day and time). Original file name: <MODEL><VERSION>.mvq <MODEL> = Name and model machine, e.g. Lua_9235... <VERSION> = Version of the software, e.g. V9.... Backup file name: <MODEL><VERSION>_YYMMDDTIME.mvq YY = year, e.g. 20 = 2020 MM = month, e.g. 01 = January DD = day, eg. 04 = 4th day of the month Load configuration from USB Standard Device 0 is available (only if a USB stick is placed). It is possible to explore the maps in the stick to find the needed configuration file. The new loaded file from the stick is selected, loaded and set as active configuration automatically. Save configuration to USB This will save the current active file to the USB stick.
notes: pen Sie auf die Taste [Backup] der gewünschten Konfigurationsdatei, um eine Backup-Kopie zu erstellen. Eine Kopie der Konfigurationsdatei mit allen Einstellungen wird erstellt. Der Name der Sicherungsdatei ist der ursprüngliche Dateiname plus ein hinzugefügter Zeitstempel (Jahr, Monat, Tag und Uhrzeit).

menu.title: Out of order message

menu.title: Scheduled Actions
menu.text: Login > Software > Scheduled actions Scheduler actions The following automatic actions can be set: • (Adaptive) Energy Save / Eco mode • Machine blocked • Free vend • Use other price list • Machine off • Mixer kick (do not change) • Daily rinse (do not change) Overview of the default (set in the factory) scheduler settings: Adaptive Energy Save If the coffee machine is connected to ConnectMe, the Energy Save mode can be made adaptive. In that case, ConnectMe monitors the use of the machine and optimizes the Energy Save values to be more in line with the actual use. Energy Save With the energy save settings, the machine can be switched to an energy saving mode (economic mode) during a period of time. During this time the boiler temperature drops to 65 ºC. When a user selects a drink, the machine will first heat to the normal temperature, before the machine is ready to give consumptions. During the warming up period the message "Heating Boiler" is shown. If the machine is not used for an hour the machine will go back to the energy save mode. Machine blocked During this set time, the functions on the front panel are blocked and not visible for the user. No consumptions can be chosen. The boiler(s) stay hot. (The service mode is still working). Switch to free vend A machine in pay mode can be switched to free vend during the set time. Check the Software -> Payment section to place the machine in Paid Mode. Use other price list In the set time the machine will switch to the other price list. Check the Products -> Price Settings section for more details. Machine off The machine is switched off during the set time. The display is completely black. The boiler elements are switched off. During this time the machine can only be activated in the service menu.

menu.title: Payment
menu.text: Login > Software > Payment When a payment unit is installed / connected, payment settings are available to set the options of the payment system. Paid vend tap the desired mode: free vend or paid mode. Multi vend a payment system can run in multi vend or single vend: • Multi vend: select and dispense one or more consumptions. Your change or card will be returned after pressing the return button on change giver or card reader. • Singe vend: select and dispense one consumption. Your change or card is returned directly after dispense of the consumption. Overpay allowed in exact change enable to allow to insert more money as the highest consumption price. Not allowed means that it is not possible to insert more money as the highest consumption price. Selected currency tap to select the active currency. Price settings - In the Service Menu, check the section Login > Products > Settings > Price Settings for details about price lists. - In clock/time settings it is possible to automatically choose between price lists and free or paid mode for a certain period of time.

Tap the [Enable/Disable] switch to activate/deactivate the PIN code entry. The usage field shows the amount of dispenses for each activated PIN code.
